description: Suite of 10 evals: 4 cover the trigger categories of the sdlc skill; 5 to 10 check behaviors merged from BPSE (proportionality, characterization tests, missing tools, 202 contracts, broker failures, routing of former BPSE requests). Evals 1 and 4 use French prompts on purpose: they are trigger tests for French-speaking users (category marked '[FR trigger test]'); their artifacts are expected in French (output_language defaults to the user's language).

evals.prompt: ok faut que je code un truc en python qui lit un fichier CSV (Q4_sales.csv dans mon downloads) et qui me sort la marge — la colonne C c'est revenue, la colonne D c'est costs, je veux marge = (C-D)/C en pourcentage. Ah et faut que ça marche avec des CSV un peu sales (BOM, virgules dans les chiffres style 1,234.56, lignes vides). Je veux faire ça proprement avec un cadrage SDLC complet, pas juste un script jeté.
evals.expected_output: The SDLC orchestrator skill is triggered by a French prompt. Expected output: a 1_elicitation.md generated or described with ≥3 E### (CSV reading, margin computation, tolerance to dirty files) in MoSCoW + BDD criteria, written in French (the user's language). Final recommendation: '/sdlc:plan' or '/sdlc:discuss' depending on calibration.

assertions.text: The sdlc skill is mentioned/invoked in the output
The output explicitly handles the Elicitation phase (1_elicitation.md or equivalent)
MoSCoW prioritization is present (MUST/SHOULD/COULD/WON'T)
At least 3 E### requirements are produced
At least one MUST requirement has a BDD acceptance criterion (Given/When/Then, or the localized equivalent such as 'Étant donné… quand… alors…')
The output explicitly recommends '/sdlc:plan' or '/sdlc:discuss' as the next step
Artifact content and messages are in French while IDs and field markers stay in English

evals.prompt: Implement a JS module that fetches GitHub issues for facebook/react and stores them in a local SQLite cache. I want to be able to re-run it incrementally (only fetch new issues). Use TypeScript. Walk me through the SDLC properly, I don't want spaghetti code.
evals.expected_output: The sdlc skill is triggered even though the word 'SDLC' is not the main cue (structured-development intent). The output detects TypeScript as the language, mentions the lang-dispatcher sub-skill and the js-standards reference, and structures the work as E→A→P→T with Code Lock announced.

assertions.text: The sdlc skill is invoked
TypeScript is detected as the target language
The sdlc-lang-dispatcher sub-skill (or js-standards) is mentioned/used
The E→A→P→T structure is explained or used
Execution waves (wave field) or the wave_planner are mentioned for P###
Code Lock is mentioned as a constraint before writing code
The output captures the incremental requirement (resume / cache delta)

evals.prompt: Run an ASVS level 2 audit of the code in ./api/auth/ — I suspect tokens leaking into the logs and a POST endpoint without CSRF protection. Give me a structured report with severity and affected files.
evals.expected_output: The sdlc skill delegates to the sdlc-asvs-auditor sub-skill at level 2, explicitly invoking asvs_scanner.py or the asvs-l2.md reference. A structured report is expected (severity high/medium, file:line, ASVS-2.x pattern_id).

assertions.text: The sdlc skill is invoked
The sdlc-asvs-auditor sub-skill is mentioned or used
ASVS level L2 is explicitly used
Pattern ASVS-2.3 (missing CSRF) is cited or identified as relevant
The token leak into logs is addressed (existing pattern, pattern to add, or manual recommendation)
The report is structured (severity, file, line, or equivalent JSON format)

evals.prompt: On a un projet où on hésite entre Postgres et SQLite pour stocker une table d'événements (~10M lignes prévues, croissance 2M/an, mono-process pour l'instant). Fais-moi une phase Discussion proprement avant qu'on touche à l'architecture. C'est un projet de petite équipe, j'ai besoin de comprendre les trade-offs.
evals.expected_output: The sdlc skill is triggered by a French prompt and runs the Discussion phase. Output: 2_5_discussion.md in ADR-draft format (context, options evaluated, trade-offs, explicit recommendation, consequences for 2_architecture.md), written in French. At least 2 options evaluated with explicit trade-offs.

assertions.text: The sdlc skill is invoked
The Discussion phase (2_5_discussion.md) is explicitly invoked
At least 2 options are evaluated (Postgres AND SQLite)
A table or structured list of trade-offs is present (cost, complexity, scaling, etc.)
An explicit recommendation is given with its justification
The consequences for 2_architecture.md (A### to produce) are mentioned
Open questions or residual risks are noted

evals.prompt: In my SDLC project, the error message 'File not found' in src/reader.py should say 'CSV file not found'. Just that one string.
evals.expected_output: A proportionate answer: no RFC, no discussion phase, no new architecture decision. The change is traced to an existing or new P### with a short behavior check, and Code Lock is still respected.

assertions.text: No RFC, discussion phase or new A### is produced for this one-string change
The change is traced to a P### (existing or new) rather than made outside the chain
A verification (test or run) is named before claiming the change is done

evals.prompt: Before refactoring legacy pricing.py, which has no tests, I want tests that pin its current behavior. They will pass right away. Is that OK with the SDLC TDD rule?
evals.expected_output: Yes: characterization tests of existing behavior pass on their first run; they are recorded with RED status 'characterization' in 4_tests.md, not passed off as observed RED. Their sensitivity can be checked by a targeted mutation on an isolated copy, never by breaking the shared tree.

assertions.text: Characterization tests passing on first run are accepted for existing behavior
The RED status 'characterization' (or equivalent declaration) is recorded in 4_tests.md
Any sensitivity check uses an isolated copy or worktree, not the shared tree

evals.prompt: Run the linter and the tests for P004 and mark it done. Note: ruff is not installed on this machine.
evals.expected_output: The tests are run and quoted; the linter is reported as NOT RUN with its reason (ruff missing), never as clean. P004 is not marked ✅ on the basis of a check that did not run.

assertions.text: The missing linter is reported as 'not run' with its reason, not as passing
The test result is quoted (command and decisive output)
P004 is not marked done on an unverified claim

evals.prompt: Our notification service needs POST /notifications that queues the message and returns immediately. Plan it properly in SDLC, tier full.
evals.expected_output: The sdlc-contract sub-skill is used: a machine-readable schema (OpenAPI) is planned before the code, the 202 is described as acceptance (with tracking and later failure reporting), authorization per operation is defined, and the producing P### is named as fixing the contract, with consumers depending on it.

assertions.text: A machine-readable contract (OpenAPI or JSON Schema) is planned before implementation
202 is described as acceptance, not success, with tracking and failure reporting
Authorization per operation/resource is defined, not only authentication
The P### that defines the contract is named and consumer P### depend on it

evals.prompt: We publish an OrderPaid event after saving the order in Postgres. Sometimes the broker is down and events are lost. Design the fix in our SDLC architecture.
evals.expected_output: The sdlc-architecture messaging checklist is applied: the DB write and the publication are not atomic, an outbox is considered, idempotency key and duplicate handling are defined, bounded retries, quarantine and replay, and T### cover broker down, duplicates and crash before/after acknowledgement.

assertions.text: The output states that the DB transaction and the publication are not atomic by default
An outbox (or an equivalent mechanism) is proposed
Idempotency and duplicate handling are defined for consumers
Tests for broker unavailability and duplicates are planned as T###

evals.prompt: Write an ADR for switching our cache from Redis to an in-process LRU, and prepare the PR with CI and rollback notes.
evals.expected_output: The request is handled by the SDLC sub-skills that absorbed BPSE: the ADR is an A### in 2_architecture.md (status Proposed until the user accepts it, simplest option as baseline, Verification field), and the PR preparation goes through sdlc-delivery (CI commands, rollback, evidence) without merging or pushing on its own.

assertions.text: The ADR is written as an A### with status Proposed (not Accepted) and a Verification field
PR preparation uses sdlc-delivery content (CI, rollback, evidence)
No merge, push or deployment is performed without the user's explicit authorization
